steps.section: A. Orientation: the four Grades tabs
steps.title: Manage Grades tab (structure)
steps.card:
WHAT: the structure tab: categories, items, maximum points, weights. Nothing here is a learner score.
Enter Grades, to its left, is the spreadsheet of learner scores. Schemes holds the letter or symbol scale. Setup Wizard sets the calculation policy.
WHY: most gradebook tickets start with knowing which of these two tabs the educator was on.
TICKET: "I changed the assignment to be out of 50 but Sarah still shows 40/100." Max points is fixed in Manage Grades; her score is fixed in Enter Grades.
NEXT: nothing to click yet; the wizard landing page is where a brand-new course opens.

steps.section: B. Undo a mistake: delete a category, reset the grading system
steps.title: More Actions (Manage Grades tab)
steps.card:
WHAT: bulk operations on the gradebook structure. On MSU's instance the menu holds Reorder, View Event Log, Make Visible to Users, Hide from Users, Delete.
WHY NOW: deleting a category or item lives here, not in the row menu. (Import and Export are under Enter Grades, not here.)
TICKET: "I can't find where to delete a grade item." Answer: Manage Grades > More Actions > Delete.
NEXT: the dropdown opens under the button.

steps.section: B. Undo a mistake: delete a category, reset the grading system
steps.title: Delete (menu item)
steps.card:
WHAT: opens the Delete Grade Items and Categories page, where you pick what to remove.
WHY: deletion is a bulk action across the whole structure, so it sits under More Actions rather than on a single row.
TICKET: "How do I remove a category I created by mistake?" Same route. If it already holds scores, stop and confirm with the educator first.
NEXT: a page with a checkbox beside each item and category.

steps.section: B. Undo a mistake: delete a category, reset the grading system
steps.title: Delete Grade Items and Categories
steps.card:
WHAT: the Delete page lists every category and item you are allowed to remove. Tick a row, then press Delete.
CAUTION: deleting an item erases every learner score stored in it. In a real course, export grades first (Enter Grades > Export).
TICKET: "I deleted a column by mistake, can you restore it?" Answer: no undo in D2L; restore from an export or re-enter.
NEXT: a confirmation prompt, then back to Manage Grades.

steps.section: B. Undo a mistake: delete a category, reset the grading system
steps.title: Confirmation dialog
steps.card:
WHAT: D2L's own warning. Deleting removes every stored score in the item, drops it from calculations, and unlinks any assignment or quiz that pointed to it.
WHY: this text is the answer to the "can you restore my column" ticket. There is no undo. D2L itself suggests hiding instead.
TICKET: "Students lost their quiz marks after I tidied the gradebook." Ask what was deleted; the scores went with it.
NEXT: Manage Grades reloads; the red note now says the final grade sums to 0%.

steps.section: B. Undo a mistake: delete a category, reset the grading system
steps.title: Settings gear (Grades tool, top right)
steps.card:
WHAT: the gradebook policy page. Three tabs: Personal Display Options (your view only), Org Unit Display Options (what students see), Calculation Options (Points / Weighted / Formula, ungraded handling, final grade type).
WHY: the same choices as the Setup Wizard, editable any time without re-running the wizard.
TICKET: "Students see letters but I want them to see points." That is Org Unit Display Options.
NEXT: the Settings page opens on Personal Display Options.

steps.section: B. Undo a mistake: delete a category, reset the grading system
steps.title: Calculation Options tab
steps.card:
WHAT: the math policy for the whole gradebook: Grading System (Points / Weighted / Formula), Final Grade Released (Calculated / Adjusted), Ungraded Items (exclude / treat as 0), automatic zeros, Auto Update.
WHY: this is where a course was set up wrong and where you fix it. Changing Points to Weighted keeps the items but adds weight fields you must fill.
TICKET: "My final grade column shows out of 240 instead of a percent." Usually Points selected when Weighted was intended, or the reverse.
NEXT: a form of radio buttons with Save at the bottom.

steps.section: B. Undo a mistake: delete a category, reset the grading system
steps.title: Grading System: Points (radio button)
steps.card:
WHAT: Points = every item adds its raw points; the final grade is earned / possible (example: /240 points).
Weighted = each category or item is a % of the final; items still need max points.
Formula = Points plus a custom rule (advanced; later lesson).
WHY: switching back to Points so the lesson restarts from the original state.
TICKET: "I want quizzes to be 40% no matter how many points they have." That is Weighted.
NEXT: Save at the bottom, then two confirmations.

steps.section: B. Undo a mistake: delete a category, reset the grading system
steps.title: Confirmation 1 of 2
steps.card:
WHAT: the first of two confirmations. The second asks: "Are you sure you want to change the Grading System for the org unit?"
WHY: changing the system recalculates every learner's final grade and changes what the Weight column means.
TICKET: "I switched to Weighted and now everyone's final grade looks wrong." Weights must be assigned after the switch; look for the red note on Manage Grades.
NEXT: the second confirmation.

steps.section: B. Undo a mistake: delete a category, reset the grading system
steps.title: Confirmation 2 of 2
steps.card:
WHAT: D2L double-checks a grading system change because it affects the org unit (this course) as a whole.
WHY: this is the point of no return for the recalculation. Nothing is saved until this Yes.
TICKET: "I clicked Save on Calculation Options but nothing changed." They closed one of the confirmations with No or the X.
NEXT: a green "Saved successfully" toast.

steps.section: B. Undo a mistake: delete a category, reset the grading system
steps.title: Verify the saved state
steps.card:
CHECK: Points is selected after the save. A toast is not proof on its own; reopen the page (or the Setup Wizard summary) to confirm the setting stuck.
RESULT in the sandbox: Grading System = Points, no categories, Final Calculated Grade weight 0.
WORKFLOW SAVED AS: delete a category (More Actions > Delete) and change grading system (Settings > Calculation Options), both institution-verified on 2026-09-22.
NEXT SECTION: the Setup Wizard, one screen at a time.
steps.actionLabel: Read only. End of section B.

steps.title: Setup Wizard: Start button
steps.card:
WHAT: the Setup Wizard walks through 7 screens of gradebook policy and ends with a summary. Above it, Current Grade Book Settings shows what is in force now (Points, calculated final grade, drop ungraded, Percentage scheme).
WHY: run it once for a new course; afterwards use the Settings gear for single changes.
TICKET: "Where do I choose weighted grading?" Either here (Step 1) or Settings > Calculation Options.
NEXT: Step 1 of 7: Choose Grading System.
steps.section: C. Setup Wizard: the seven policy screens

steps.title: Step 1 of 7: Grading System = Weighted
steps.card:
WHAT: Weighted means every top-level category or item is a percentage of the final grade, and they must add up to 100%. Inside a category, item weights are percentages of that category.
Points (currently selected) means raw points add up; the final is earned / possible.
Formula is Points plus a custom expression; leave for a later lesson.
WHY: the lab uses Weighted so we can see how a 10-point quiz can still be worth 20% of the course.
TICKET: "Weights add up but the note says not 100%." Only top-level rows count toward 100; items inside a category count toward the category.
NEXT: Continue goes to Step 2: Final Grade Released.
steps.section: C. Setup Wizard: the seven policy screens

steps.title: Step 2 of 7: Final Grade Released
steps.card:
WHAT: which final-grade column students will eventually see. Calculated = D2L computes it from the items and keeps it current. Adjusted = a column the instructor types or copies into, then edits by hand (rounding, curving).
You can release only one of the two.
WHY: keep Calculated for the lab; Adjusted comes in the calculated-vs-adjusted section later.
TICKET: "I bumped a student to 90 but they still see 89.4." The course releases Calculated, and the edit went into Adjusted (or the reverse).
BELOW: Automatically release final grade. Leave it off; releasing is a deliberate step we practise later.
NEXT: Step 3: Grade Calculations.
steps.actionLabel: Keep Calculated Final Grade, click Continue
steps.section: C. Setup Wizard: the seven policy screens

steps.title: Step 3 of 7: Grade Calculations
steps.card:
WHAT: how a blank cell counts. Drop ungraded items = a blank is left out of the denominator, so the running total reflects only graded work. Treat ungraded items as 0 = a blank counts as zero, so the running total looks like a final grade all term.
Below: Automatically apply a grade of zero to missing submissions once overdue (present on MSU, off by default, future due dates only). Auto Update = recalculate the final grade every time a score changes.
WHY: keep Drop ungraded for the lab so we can show both behaviours with the same data.
TICKET: "Everyone's grade dropped 30% overnight." Someone switched to Treat as 0 with blanks still in the book. MSU's tip: enter earned zeros instead.
NEXT: Step 4: Default Grade Scheme.
steps.actionLabel: Keep Drop ungraded items, click Continue
steps.section: C. Setup Wizard: the seven policy screens

steps.title: Step 4 of 7: Default Grade Scheme
steps.card:
WHAT: a grade scheme maps a percentage to a symbol (letter, 4.0 value, Pass). It changes how a grade is displayed, never how it is calculated.
Only the organization scheme Percentage exists in this course. Course schemes are made on the Schemes tab (we build a 4.0-style one later).
WHY: the default scheme applies to every item and to the final grade unless an item overrides it.
TICKET: "Students see 3.5 on one quiz and 87% on another." One item has its own scheme; check Manage Grades > item > Display Options.
NEXT: Step 5: Managing View Display Options.
steps.section: C. Setup Wizard: the seven policy screens

steps.target: Number of decimal places to display
steps.title: Step 5 of 7: Managing View Display Options
steps.card:
WHAT: Step 5 has one setting: decimals shown to YOU in Enter Grades (default 2). It does not round the stored value.
WHY: leave at 2. Rounding disputes usually come from the student-facing decimals on the next screen, not this one.
TICKET: "The gradebook shows 89.5 but the student sees 90." Compare the managing-view decimals (here) with the student-view decimals (Step 6).
NEXT: Step 6: Student View Display Options.
steps.section: C. Setup Wizard: the seven policy screens

steps.target: Display final grade calculation to users
steps.title: Step 6 of 7: Student View Display Options
steps.card:
WHAT: what students see on each grade: Points grade (8/10), Weighted grade (16/20 of the course), Grade scheme symbol (letter or 4.0), Grade scheme color. Plus decimals, text length, and this checkbox.
This checkbox shows students a small calculator icon with the breakdown of their final grade. It is NOT the same as releasing the final grade; MSU's tips page makes the same distinction.
WHY: leave it off for now; we switch it on in the visibility section.
TICKET: "Students can see the calculation but not the final grade" or the reverse: two separate settings.
NEXT: Step 7: summary, then Finish.
steps.section: C. Setup Wizard: the seven policy screens

steps.title: Step 7 of 7: Summary and Finish
steps.card:
WHAT: the summary lists every choice; nothing is saved until Finish.
CHECK before clicking: Weighted; Release the Calculated Final Grade; Do not automatically release; Drop ungraded items; Automatically keep final grades updated; Percentage scheme.
TICKET: "I ran the wizard but my settings did not change." They pressed Cancel or closed the tab on step 7.
NEXT: a Grade Options page with links to create a category, an item, a scheme, or enter grades.
steps.section: C. Setup Wizard: the seven policy screens

steps.title: Grade Options (wizard finished)
steps.card:
CHECK: the toast says Saved successfully and the Grade Options links appear. The same links exist as New > Category / New > Item on Manage Grades.
RESULT in the sandbox: Weighted, Calculated, not auto-released, Drop ungraded, auto-update on, Percentage. Verified on the wizard summary screen.
NEXT SECTION: build the structure: Quizzes category (40%), Q1 and Q2 (10 points each, evenly weighted), Project item (100 points, 60%).
steps.actionLabel: Read only. End of section C.
